findings.claim: The real `mini-sycophancy-correction` check never resolves or reads any `skill.toml`, so a non-local gateway configuration is silently reported as pass.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion 2.1 specifies `mini-sycophancy-correction` must `fail when the resolved skill.toml names a gateway other than http://localhost:4000/v1`, but the implementation only checks `const tomlPath = ctx.skillToml?.() ?? null;` and has no default resolver, so outside injected tests `tomlPath` is always null and the gateway branch never runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a real default resolver for the sycophancy skill.toml associated with the resolved binary/skill install, or explicitly skip with a reason when the config location cannot be resolved instead of passing.

findings.claim: `mini-install-scope` cannot detect stale mini skill copies in real runs because retired skill names are only accepted through an injected test-only `ctx.alsoMine` list.
findings.evidence: The spec says `mini-install-scope` SHALL fail when the full pack is present and `any mini skill copy exists under either home skills root`; the implementation builds candidates from `new Set([...listSkillNames(), ...(ctx.alsoMine ?? [])])`, while `scripts/doctor.mjs` only passes `{ home }` as context and never supplies `alsoMine` or any install manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Persist and read an install manifest of names previously written by the mini, or otherwise provide a real runtime source for retired mini skill names before claiming stale copies are enforced.
